body:
INDEPENDENT SCIENTIFIC ATTACK — REVISION REQUIRED before candidate review.

Snapshot reviewed: untracked 331-line draft, SHA-256 09a6924882eaa7cdf726fef690e9d1bdad581e5c5696acc803dfcab8d39047cf; git diff --check clean.

The draft does satisfy the original checklist: it defines both floor-error directions, full-path reruns, the eight-cell macro estimand, story-family split, established roster, honest null and identified set, provider/geometry/cost/transition/source identities, separate candidate recall/path decision/model-relative P-F/probability calibration, Unranked support accounting, independent hashed-ngram and TF-IDF arms, WOG 1.480580357 as diagnostic only, and no retuning.

Five findings remain:

1. BLOCKING — oracle discourse leakage is not forbidden. DefaultLocalCostModel consumes RecallUnit.function twice: FunctionPrior changes every source cost and ExternalStates.natural chooses which external state gets the floor (cost.scala:715-763). The adjudication protocol separately defines GoldUnit.discourse as an oracle label, with predicted labels scored separately (fixture-adjudication protocol:153-163). The court freezes a discourse-function checksum but never says whether inference receives the unattended prediction or the oracle. If oracle Association, Inference, or Uninterpretable is copied into RecallUnit.function, the model receives part of the answer used to score the floor. Remedy: freeze separate identities for model-input discourse and oracle gold; require model input to come from the untouched unattended path or a declared cross-fitted predictor; add a mutation that substitutes oracle discourse and must fail admission.

2. BLOCKING — Inference currently uses one target field for two incompatible meanings. WogBench.goldFor creates Groundedness.Inference with nonempty targets and primary (wog.scala:91-100). GoldUnit documents those as acceptable anchors, while court:182-185 says every non-source unit predicted source is a false-source error. Thus the same source node is both an acceptable target and an error if selected. Remedy: separate a related-source/evidence target from an acceptable alignment target, or explicitly remove inference targets from the primary binary acceptance set. The published field must distinguish the two meanings.

3. BLOCKING — Uninterpretable is not evidence of external origin. The court treats all four external cells, including uninterpretable, as gold-negative for source anchoring. If content cannot be interpreted, a source anchor has not been falsified; scoring it as false-source turns adjudication uncertainty into a participant outcome. Keep Uninterpretable in the frozen denominator and report it, but treat it as adjudication/support indeterminacy for the binary estimand unless a separate observation establishes external origin.

4. REQUIRED ESTIMAND CORRECTION — the weighting formula is family -> recall -> unit, but lines 101-104 allow participants to recur and lines 200-202 claim a prolific participant cannot dominate. A participant contributing several recalls receives several votes inside a family. Either add participant as an averaging level, freeze one eligible recall per participant per family, or narrow the claim. Participant-clustered uncertainty alone does not repair the point estimand.

5. BLOCKING EXECUTION PRECONDITION from the chiefs 16:49 audit gap — the identity table names nomination receipts, but current GraphHsmm.infer passes only anchorsByUnit into HsmmResult and discards channel, rank, score, space, and receipt (hsmm.scala:523-535; candidates.scala:26-35). Until a checked nomination packet or complete fingerprint survives into HsmmResult and wire identity, the court cannot prove which candidate process it calibrated. Add the explicit precondition and the court: same anchors with different lawful nomination provenance must have different calibration identities while P and F remain numerically unchanged.

I do not approve the current bytes. These are scope-preserving edits to the pre-data court, not requests for API or implementation in this bead.
